title: Customer edge connection evidence spec (PRD sketch)
content:
PURPOSE
This is a working PRD sketch for a compact, machine-friendly "evidence" format to attach to customer-managed networking events during Private deployments. Surface goals are: make approval gates auditable, allow simple end-to-end forensic queries, and keep telemetry compact enough for customers that ship logs to their own SIEMs.

Context / Problem statement
- In Private deployments customers operate their own VPCs / on-prem networks while Redwood runs a control plane or a lightweight agent. 
- Current audit log outputs are siloed: operator audit entries, control-plane events, and connectivity attestations are in separate schemas. This makes:
  - postmortem stitching slow (have to correlate across multiple IDs),
  - approval gates hard to validate automatically,
  - customers asking for a single artifact to prove a change was authorized and traceable.
- We need a minimal, signed evidence bundle that can be generated at the time of an approval gate transition and attached to both (a) the internal audit log and (b) the customer-facing handover logs.

Goals
- Define a compact JSON Line event schema (evidence-event) suitable for streaming and for storing in object blobs.
- Ensure event contains the minimum set of fields to prove: who approved, what authority was checked, which CIDR/route change was applied, and a cryptographic proof (sig or hash) of the bundle.
- Provide an approval-state machine diagram and the gate check sequence for operator + customer-managed paths.
- Outline integration points: control plane, agent, operator console, customer handover package, and SSO/KMS for signing.

Non-goals
- This PRD will not specify storage retention policies (separate compliance doc).
- Does not design full UI polish for console; focus is data model + minimal UX hooks.

User stories (examples)
- As an SRE at Customer X, I want a single log artifact I can ingest into Splunk to prove a route change was approved by a named admin and vetted by the customer's network ACL check.
- As Redwood on-call, I want to quickly fetch the evidence bundle for the last 24h of changes for a tenant to expedite incident triage.
- As a security reviewer, I want to validate that approval gates cannot be bypassed and that each gate state transition includes an immutable event with a signature.

Proposed solution (high level)
1) Evidence-event schema (newline-delimited JSON): each evidence-event is one atomic artifact representing a gate transition or a handoff. Fields (minimal):
   - event_id (uuid)
   - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
   - tenant_id
   - resource (string) e.g., "vpc-attach", "route-update", "edge-tunnel"
   - change_summary (short string)
   - requested_by (principal id/email)
   - approver (principal id/email)  // null if automated
   - approval_method (manual | policy-allow | delegated-token)
   - policy_reference (optional string: policy id or hash)
   - pre_change_snapshot (short hash or small text blob pointing to pre-change metadata)
   - post_change_snapshot (short hash)
   - artifacts (list of URIs or object keys)  // can point to more detailed dumps in object storage
   - evidence_digest (sha256 hex)  // computed over canonicalized event+artifacts listing
   - signer_id (key id)
   - signature (base64)  // signature over evidence_digest using signer_id key (KMS/HSM)
   - related_ids (list of ids)  // cross-links to control-plane audit ids, ticket ids, PRs
   - ttl_hint (string) // e.g., "retention:1y" - advisory only

Notes on schema choices:
- Keep most fields short; large snapshots are referenced by artifact URIs rather than embedded. Aim for ~2KB per event on average.
- events are append-only. Modifications are modeled by creating a new evidence-event that references prior event_id in related_ids.
- signature model is pluggable: for hosted we use Redwood KMS key; for private we support customer-managed signer (customer KMS key or SSH signing key injected during onboarding).

Approval gate sequence (happy path)
1) Change requested (agent or control-plane). Evidence-event created with approval_method="pending" and pre_change_snapshot recorded.
2) Policy check executed (customer policy or Redwood default). If pass -> approver populated (policy-allow) else -> manual approval requested.
3) Manual approver signs via console or CLI (this writes approver, approval_method=manual, signs the evidence_digest).
4) Agent applies change, records post_change_snapshot, updates evidence-event, recomputes evidence_digest and appends signature.
5) Final evidence-event is surfaced to: internal audit index, customer handover bundle (object store + pointer in tenant console), and optionally streamed to customer SIEM.

Edge cases and failure modes
- Agent offline when approver signs: allow signing before agent applies change; final event must reference the applying agent id and include agent-ack signature when applied.
- Partial apply: evidence-event should include a partial_apply boolean and a list of failed sub-steps.
- Signature rotation: when signer key rotates, create a new event with signer_id set to new key and related_ids referencing earlier evidence.

Operational and privacy considerations
- By default, redact sensitive IPs or internal hostnames in customer-facing bundles unless customer opts into full export. Add a flag export_level: minimal | full.
- For private deployments where customers require air-gapped proof, support an offline signing mode where Redwood provides a signing CLI that the customer runs against the canonicalized event (returns signature blob to the control plane).

Integration points (who touches this)
- Control plane: orchestrates gate flow, writes initial event records, stores artifact pointers.
- Edge agent: responsible for pre/post snapshots, agent-level ack signature, and applying changes.
- Console/CLI: manual approver flows; UI shows event status and allows signing/approve actions.
- KMS/HSM: signing and verification. Support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed keys.
- Telemetry/indexer: index evidence-events into per-tenant audit index and support fast query APIs (by event_id, tenant_id, resource, time range).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics
- Evidence-event schema committed and validated with 3 integration teams (agent, control-plane, console) by end of Q1.
- Average evidence-event size < 4KB in production for normal route changes.
- <2s median time to generate final evidence-event after change completes (control-plane metric).
- Customers can configure streaming to external SIEM within 1 business day of GA.

Rollout plan (staged)
- Phase 0 (spec + prototype): design canonicalization and sample signing workflow; CLI thin-client for offline sign (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (internal): wire into control-plane and agent in a feature flag; route changes for a small set of beta tenants (4 weeks).
- Phase 2 (customer beta): invite 3 customers for hands-on trial; add SIEM streaming configuration (6 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): integrate with onboarding playbook, add docs & runbook, default retention guidance (4 weeks).

UI / UX notes (quick sketches)
- Approval modal shows: change_summary, pre/post snapshot diff (collapsed), approver, signature status.
- Evidence bundle download button: returns a signed tarball with event.json + artifact pointers + signature metadata.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we canonicalize artifacts referenced by URI so evidence_digest is stable across object-store provider differences? (TODO: canonicalization design doc).
- What is the minimum policy_reference representation for complex network policies? Hash + human-readable?
- Decide format for partial_apply reporting (list vs map).
- Determine default export_level and privacy opt-ins for EU customers (GDPR implications).

Dependencies
- KMS team: support for cross-tenant signing and rotation APIs.
- Agent team: small footprint change to compute pre/post snapshot and to return ack signatures.
- Console: approval modal and signed artifact download.
- Billing/Legal: validation of retention and export language for customer handover.

Appendix: example evidence-event (canonicalized, pretty-printed)
{
  "event_id": "e3f8d6a2-6b2e-4a9f-b8f2-5a9c1de9e7a4",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-21T15:12:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-341",
  "resource": "route-update",
  "change_summary": "Add route 10.40.0.0/16 -> edge-tunnel-7",
  "requested_by": "alice@custco.com",
  "approver": "netops-bot@custco.com",
  "approval_method": "policy-allow",
  "policy_reference": "policy:net-allow-2025-11-hash:abc123",
  "pre_change_snapshot": "sha256:0a1b2c...",
  "post_change_snapshot": "sha256:dd4f5e...",
  "artifacts": ["s3://cust-logs/tenant-341/changes/e3f8d6a2/meta.json"],
  "evidence_digest": "sha256:9f8b7a...",
  "signer_id": "redwood-kms:keys/global-edge-signing-v1",
  "signature": "MEUCIQD...base64...",
  "related_ids": ["audit-98234", "JIRA-PRIVNET-142"],
  "ttl_hint": "retention:1y"
}

Notes to reviewers
- Please add comments inline for the schema fields you think are unnecessary/too heavyweight.
- Stakes: this artifact becomes the canonical handoff we give customers when they ask: "show me proof the change was authorized". Need a balance between minimal size and legal defensibility.

Quick action items
- [ ] Security: pick signature envelope format (JOSE vs raw signature)
- [ ] Agent: prototype pre/post snapshot CLI call
- [ ] Control-plane: draft canonicalization rules and hashing algorithm
- [ ] Product: draft onboarding checklist for customer-managed keys

End of sketch.
